info.title: XERJ REST API — agent core (partial spec)
info.summary: Core index, ingest, search, and agent-memory endpoints for XERJ.
info.description: XERJ is an Elasticsearch-compatible search engine written in Rust. This document covers the core REST surface that backs the six canonical agent operations: index creation, document ingest (single and bulk), search (lexical, semantic, vector/kNN, and hybrid), and namespaced agent memory (store + recall). The search endpoint is a single verb whose behaviour is selected by the request body: a `semantic` query for meaning-based recall, a top-level `knn` clause for vector search, or a `hybrid` query for score fusion. Semantic and semantic-memory features use XERJ's built-in embedder and require no external embedding provider or API key. Unfiltered vector (kNN) search is served by a persisted HNSW graph (approximate) with exact rescoring of candidates — measured recall@10 1.00 on the official bench query, 100-probe mean 0.976; num_candidates sets the beam width (floored at 800). Filtered kNN and other ineligible shapes (non-cosine, SQ8, indexes under 1,024 docs) run an exact brute-force scan (recall 1.00). SCOPE: this document is deliberately partial. It specifies the 7 routes behind those six operations, not XERJ's REST surface, which is more than 200 routes wide. The version above describes this document, not the engine — read an endpoint's absence here as "not written up yet", never as "not supported". The complete wire contract is the one the ES-compat YAML conformance suite exercises (engine/tests/es-compat-yaml).

put.description: Create an index with optional mappings and settings. To enable semantic search, map a field as `semantic_text` (XERJ auto-embeds it at ingest with the built-in embedder). To enable vector/kNN search, map a `dense_vector` field with `dims` set to your embedding dimension.

semantic_and_vector.summary: Index with a semantic_text field and a dense_vector field

post.description: Index a single JSON document; the id is auto-generated. Fields mapped as `semantic_text` are embedded server-side at ingest so they become recallable by meaning.

value.title: VPN outage postmortem
value.body: Users could not connect to the corporate VPN for 40 minutes.

put.summary: Index a document with an explicit id
put.description: Create or overwrite a document at the given id.

post.summary: Search an index (lexical, semantic, vector, or hybrid)
post.description: Single search endpoint whose behaviour is selected by the request body. Use a Query DSL clause in `query` for lexical/structured search, a `semantic` query for meaning-based recall over a `semantic_text` field, a top-level `knn` clause for vector search over a `dense_vector` field, or a `hybrid` query to fuse multiple sub-queries with RRF or linear fusion. Aggregations cannot be combined with a hybrid query.

semantic.summary: Semantic search over a semantic_text field (xerj_semantic_search)

semantic.query: how do I connect to the vpn

rerank.summary: Rerank the top hits with an external judge (sends document text off the machine; needs an operator-configured provider key)

200.description: Search results. With `rerank`, read `_rerank.applied`: a provider that missed its deadline still yields a 200, with the engine's order.

403.description: `rerank` only: the operator disabled reranking (`[rerank] enabled = false`). Nothing was sent. Error type `rerank_exception`.

502.description: `rerank` only: the provider was called and the contract broke (rejected key, malformed body, unreachable). No hits are returned. Error type `rerank_exception`.

503.description: `rerank` only: no provider key is configured on this node. Nothing was sent. Repeat the search without `rerank`. Error type `rerank_exception`.

get.description: Reports whether the `rerank` search stage can run on this node: whether a provider key is set and where it came from (`config` or `env`), the endpoint with userinfo/query/fragment removed, and the server-side limits. NEVER returns the key. Superuser only, like the rest of the `/_xerj/*` operator namespace; a caller without superuser rights learns the same thing from a `rerank` search: HTTP 503 means no key, 403 means disabled.

post.description: Bulk endpoint using newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each operation is two lines: an action line (`index`, `create`, `update`, or `delete`) followed by the source document (omitted for `delete`). The body must be sent as `application/x-ndjson` and terminated by a trailing newline.

schema.description: Newline-delimited JSON. One action line per operation, optionally followed by a source line.

200.description: Per-item results. Inspect `errors` and each item's status.

post.description: Persist a memory into a namespaced agent-memory store (xerj_memory_store). The text is stored in a `semantic_text` field and auto-embedded by the built-in embedder so it is recallable by meaning with no external embedding service. Namespaces isolate memories from one another.

value.text: The customer prefers email over phone contact.
The customer prefers email over phone contact.

200.description: Deduplicated — a near-duplicate memory already exists; the existing entry is returned.

post.description: Recall the most relevant memories from a namespace (xerj_memory_recall). Three retrieval modes are chosen by input: supply a `vector` for kNN over your own embedding; set `semantic: true` with a `query` for server-side embedded recall (no external key); or pass just `query` for BM25 text recall. An optional metadata `filter` narrows the set and `recency_weight` blends recency into the ranking.

semantic_recall.summary: Server-side semantic recall (no external embedding key)

value.query: how does the customer want to be contacted

hits.text: The customer prefers email over phone contact.

ApiKey.description: Optional API-key authentication via the `Authorization` header. XERJ accepts both `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`. Authentication is disabled by default; when it is not enabled, requests without an `Authorization` header are accepted (hence the empty top-level security requirement).

IndexPath.name: index
IndexPath.description: Index name. May be a single index, a comma-separated list, or a wildcard pattern for search.

NamespacePath.name: namespace
NamespacePath.description: Agent-memory namespace. Starts with a lowercase letter or digit; allowed characters are a-z, 0-9, '_', '-', '.' (max 200 chars).

Error.description: Error. XERJ returns an Elasticsearch-shaped error envelope.

CreateIndexBody.description: Index definition. Both fields are optional.

mappings.description: Field mappings. Use type `semantic_text` for semantic search and `dense_vector` (with `dims`) for vector/kNN search.

Document.description: An arbitrary JSON document whose fields conform to the index mapping.

SearchBody.description: Search request. Provide a `query` clause and/or a top-level `knn` clause. The `query` may itself be a `semantic` or `hybrid` clause.

query.description: An Elasticsearch Query DSL clause. Supports standard clauses (match, term, terms, range, bool, prefix, wildcard, exists, multi_match) plus XERJ's `semantic` and `hybrid` clauses.

size.description: Maximum number of hits to return.

from.description: Offset of the first hit, for pagination.

_source.description: Which source fields to return: true/false, or an array of field names.

aggs.description: Aggregations. Not supported together with a hybrid query.

track_total_hits.description: true/false, or an integer cap, controlling exact total-hit counting.

RerankBlock.description: XERJ extension: optional second-stage reranking. NOT an Elasticsearch key. PRIVACY: this is the only search-time feature that sends document text off the node - the question and the text of up to `window` hits are POSTed to a third-party relevance judge (proxy embeddings via `[embedding] default_endpoint` and the WAL tap also send text off the node when an operator configures them; docs/RERANK.md lists every outbound connection a node can open). Only fields the response returns are sent, so `_source` filtering also limits what leaves. NEEDS A CONFIGURED PROVIDER: the node's operator must have set a key (`[rerank] api_key` or TYPESAFE_API_KEY); there is no per-request key. The judge returns a calibrated probability (0..1) per document, which REPLACES `_score`; `hits.total` and `aggregations` still describe the full match set. Cannot be combined with `sort`, `search_after`, `collapse`, scroll (open or continuation) or `size: 0`, and is refused (not ignored) on _msearch, search templates, _async_search, the native search API and gRPC; `null` is the same as absent. When applied, every hit's `_score` is a probability or null (no verdict), never an engine score beside probabilities. `{}` uses every default. Unknown keys are refused by name. Ranking quality with the provider's model has not been verified by the XERJ project.

provider.description: `none`/`disabled` skips the call and reports `applied: false`.

window.description: How many of the engine's top hits are judged. Every one is a paid judgement. `from` + `size` must be <= `window`.

min_score.description: Drop hits whose relevance probability is below this. Distinct from the top-level `min_score`, which is applied to engine scores first.

query.description: The question documents are judged against (at most 4,000 characters, also when it is inferred). Inferred from `match`, `match_phrase`, `multi_match`, `semantic` and `simple_query_string`; REQUIRED for anything else (`bool`, `hybrid`, a top-level `knn` with no text query).

fields.description: EXHAUSTIVE list of returned fields to send. `["body"]` sends the body and nothing else, not even the title. Default: the title, the matching passage if returned, every other returned top-level string field of `_source`, then string values returned under the hit's `fields` that `_source` did not already return.

instructions.description: Overrides what 'relevant' means for this corpus. At most 2,000 characters: the provider's wire format repeats it inside every per-document question, so it is sent once per judged document.

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole stage. Exceeding it DEGRADES: HTTP 200 with the engine's order and `_rerank.applied: false`.

max_doc_chars.description: Title and text are each cut to this many characters.

batch.description: Documents per provider call. Values above 30 are lowered to 30.

max_concurrency.description: Provider calls in flight at once.

RerankInfo.description: Present only when the request carried `rerank`. Emitted BEFORE `hits` on the wire. Always read `applied`.

applied.description: true: the order is the judge's. false: the provider missed the deadline (or `provider` was `none`) and the order and scores are the engine's; see `reason`.

reason.description: Why reranking was not applied. Only when `applied` is false.

window.description: Hits considered: min(rerank.window, hits the engine returned).

judged.description: Documents the provider returned a verdict for - one per document; answers for documents not sent in that call are not counted.

unjudged.description: Hits in the response with no verdict: `_score` is null and they sort after every judged hit.

skipped_no_text.description: Window hits with no text in the response. Not sent.

dropped_unjudged.description: With `min_score` set, unjudged hits cannot be shown to clear the bar and are dropped.

partial_failures.description: Provider calls that did not deliver a verdict while others did: failed calls, and calls the deadline stopped from being sent.

fields_without_text.description: Only when non-empty: names in `rerank.fields` that no hit in the window returned text for.

usage.description: Tokens the provider reported for this search. Advisory: a count the provider reports as anything but a non-negative number meters as 0.

query.description: The question that was judged, inferred or given.

took_ms.description: Time spent in the stage; the response's `took` includes it.

RerankStatus.description: Whether a rerank provider is configured. Never contains the key.

enabled.description: false when the operator set `[rerank] enabled = false`.

configured.description: enabled AND a key is set.

url.description: Userinfo, query string and fragment removed.

limits.description: Server-side ceilings on the caller-chosen cost knobs: `max_docs_per_call`, `max_window`, `max_concurrency`, `max_doc_chars`, `max_timeout_ms`, and the string ceilings `max_instructions_chars`, `max_query_chars`, `max_model_chars`, `max_fields`, `max_field_name_chars`. A value over a ceiling is a 400 naming the field.

KnnClause.description: ES 8.x top-level kNN clause. Unfiltered kNN is HNSW-served with exact rescoring; filtered kNN runs the exact brute-force scan.

query_vector.description: Query embedding; length must equal the field's mapped `dims`.

k.description: Number of nearest neighbours to return.

num_candidates.description: Optional candidate-pool size before selecting top k.

text.description: The memory text. Indexed for BM25 and auto-embedded for semantic recall.

metadata.description: Optional arbitrary metadata; recall can pre-filter under the `metadata.` prefix.

vector.description: Optional caller-supplied embedding, stored as a dense_vector for kNN recall.

id.description: Optional explicit id; a UUID is generated when omitted.

dedup_threshold.description: Cosine-similarity threshold used when dedup is true.

query.description: Query text for BM25 recall, or the string embedded server-side when `semantic` is true (required in semantic mode).

vector.description: Optional query embedding; runs kNN and takes precedence over query/semantic.

semantic.description: Embed `query` server-side and recall by similarity. Requires non-empty `query`. Ignored when `vector` is given.

filter.description: Optional ES query clause pre-filter over metadata.

recency_weight.description: Optional recency blend in [0,1]. 0 = pure relevance (default when omitted), 1 = pure recency.
